title: Let documents.mjs revision --check name a check the change's coverage adds
description:
Found 2026-09-27 recording readable-views-2's receipts: `node .shady2k/documents.mjs revision --check views-check` fails with 'the policy has no check views-check' although a change's Coverage may name checks the policy does not list (views-check, readability), whose receipts stand on the whole revision. The refusal hint of runCheck already prints the whole revision for them. Worked around by recording those receipts against `documents.mjs revision`.

## Done when
revision --check <id> prints the whole revision for an id the policy does not pin (or refuses only an id no policy entry and no coverage could name, saying so), a test covers it, and the integration's receipt instructions say which command to use.

title: A branch push starts only the workflows its change needs, and a newer push cancels the branch's older runs
description:
The owner, 2026-10-15 ~23:30, with a screenshot of the Actions list: «Это перебор с CI». In 15 minutes one worker branch (release/madarch-lfhu-2) pushed six small fixes; each push started four workflows (CI's five test shards, clean install walks on three OSes, release, Product documents), none cancelled when the next push superseded it, most of them red. Causes in the workflows on main (195aaff5):
- No workflow has a `concurrency` group, so superseded runs of the same branch keep running.
- `clean-installs.yml` runs on every push to every branch (`push: branches: ['**']`), whatever changed, and has no `workflow_dispatch` to run it on demand.
- `release.yml` runs on any branch push that touches release.yml, and fails there by design (no tag).

## Done when
- Every workflow has `concurrency: { group: <workflow>-<ref>, cancel-in-progress: <true except on main and tags> }`: a new push to a branch cancels that branch's older runs of the same workflow; main and tag runs are never cancelled.
- `clean-installs.yml` runs on: pushes to main, tags `v*`, pull requests that touch install-related paths (scripts/install*, the Homebrew formula and tap script, release.yml, clean-installs.yml, the walk scripts, package.json), and `workflow_dispatch`; not on every branch push.
- `release.yml` on a branch or pull request validates without the publish job counting as a failure (a skipped publish, not a red run); it publishes only on `v*` tags.
- Proven on the PR itself: two quick pushes leave one run of each workflow; the PR's list shows no red release run.
- The worker rules say: iterate a cross-OS walk with `gh workflow run`, push once when it is green.

## Left out
- Changing what the jobs test.
close_reason: Accepted on merge 86b420841f1f4057bc19758cd11623d759874bd1; post-merge CI, release validation, clean-install and document/backlog gates passed.

description:
Related work: `madarch-xq0v`. This is deferred test debt from its diagnostic home-kind Stryker run, not a merge blocker.

title: Skip the product checks in CI for changes that cannot touch the product, and run once per pull request
description:
Found in the setup 0.33.0 run (madarch-np7): CI runs bun install, check, test and views:check (about 7 minutes) on every push, documents- and tracker-only pushes included, and twice on a branch with an open pull request (push and pull_request).

## Done when
A push or pull request that changes only docs/, .beads/, .shady2k/, .githooks/ or root *.md files runs no product check; pushes run the checks on main only and pull requests once each; the integration's CI line says so.
close_reason: Fixed in e967601: CI on pushes to main and pull requests, skipping non-product paths.

title: A page's links, cross-references and footer navigate, and the reader can always go back, not only through the sidebar
description:
What a person does: opens a document page and clicks a link in its text, a backlink, a footer entry, or wants to return. What happens: per the owner nothing responds to a click inside the page; only the left sidebar moves you. What should happen: every link to another document opens it, backlinks and footer entries navigate, the browser's back returns, and a breadcrumb or the overview link is one click away. Owner: 'Перешел куда-нибудь внутрь, потом вернуться невозможно, потому что ни футеры, никакие клики не работают … только в левой панельке можно перейти.'
## DONE WHEN
On the demo product, a body link, a backlink and each footer entry open their target; browser back and forward follow; a test drives each in the built app.
## Left out
New kinds of links.

The owner, 2026-10-13, on the served demo wiki (Fieldnote): "Получается, что это неюзабельно сейчас."
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Clicking the sidebar logo marked `madarch вики` opens the Product overview.
- [x] Each visible top-bar breadcrumb segment is independently clickable and opens its represented level: `Продукт` opens the Product overview; `Fieldnote` opens its product group. These breadcrumb links provide the visible in-app way back; the Product overview stays one click away.
- [x] The generic group page is `/g/<encoded-group>`, keyed by the existing `PageMeta.kind ?? groupOf(path)` identity. It uses the existing localized/fallback group label as its heading and lists only that group’s live pages as links. The group breadcrumb segment and sidebar group heading link to it; the logo and first breadcrumb segment open the overview. No product-specific data is hard-coded.
notes: Owner Addendum 3 (2026-10-13) resolves the earlier group-route blocker: implement the generic `/g/<encoded-group>` page using the existing group identity/label and live pages only; wire both group breadcrumb and sidebar group heading to it, while logo and first breadcrumb go to overview.
close_reason: done

title: Isolate every test run in its own scratch home and temporary folder, so no suite leaves anything in the owner's home or the system temporary folder
description:
Found 2026-09-30 during the wiki run: about 87 000 folders named madarch-* had piled up in the system temporary folder (63 490 of them madarch-model-check-*), left by test suites outside the wiki (test/model-check-repo.ts fixtures and others); together with other projects' caches the disk reached 99-100% twice in one night. The wiki's own suites were fixed in madarch-7br.3.2; the rest were not in that task's scope.

Widened 2026-10-09 (owner): during madarch-rtr.2.3 a test ran `madarch new` without a scratch home and left 377 draft folders in the owner's real ~/madarch/products. Cleanliness that depends on each test remembering to redirect its paths fails again; the run as a whole must be isolated.

## Approach (owner's choice, 2026-10-09)
A test preload declared in bunfig.toml (`[test] preload`) creates one fresh scratch folder per `bun test` run and points HOME, MADARCH_HOME and TMPDIR (and any other home-derived path madarch reads, such as MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE) into it before any test file loads, and removes it when the run ends. Spawned commands inherit it. A container was considered and set aside: tests spawn git, bun and Chromium, which a container would have to carry, and CI would differ from local runs.

## Done when
after bun test (full suite, performance tests included) nothing new exists in the owner's home (~/madarch included) or in the system temporary folder, apart from the wiki's content-keyed caches if they are kept on purpose (a check before and after); a test that writes to a home or temporary path without redirecting it lands in the run's scratch folder; the scratch folder is gone after the run, pass or fail; a committed test proves the preload is active (HOME and MADARCH_HOME point inside the scratch folder).

The shared disk reached 98% (8.2 GB free of 394 GB) and the overnight worker wave of the self-filling milestone stopped around 01:50 MSK. Removing them freed 70 GB (80% used after).

A plain `rm -rf` as the same user could not remove several hundred of them: tests make subfolders unwritable and never restore them — `docs/hypotheses` and `docs/repositories/library/stories` under madarch-stages-*, `docs/private` under madarch-wiki-pages-*, `dark-draft` under madarch-cli-list-dark-*.

Criterion: after a focused run of any one test file, and after a full `bun test`, `/tmp` holds no new madarch-* entry, passing or failing; a test that removes permissions restores them in its cleanup. Disproved by any madarch-* folder left in /tmp after a run.

title: madarch keeps its fact log, graph queries and vector index in PostgreSQL everywhere: embedded PGlite locally, PostgreSQL on the server; LadybugDB and the local SQLite retired
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-15 ~00:20 MSK (decision record 0024, amending 0009 and 0023). Local mode runs PGlite (Postgres in WebAssembly, in-process, no native addon); the server runs PostgreSQL; one Postgres dialect for the bitemporal fact log, graph traversals written with WITH RECURSIVE, and pgvector. LadybugDB and the local SQLite fact log go; the graph is derived and rebuilt, so no data migration. Performance is not prototyped first (owner: «я бы пока не беспокоился о производительности, если что потом доработаемся»).

Why now: LadybugDB 0.20.4's Windows x64 addon fails to load under Bun 1.4.2 (hosted run 38636092758; Node loads the same bytes), which blocks madarch-lfhu.2's Windows outcome; it also forces a system OpenSSL dependency (89 MB binary).

## DONE WHEN
Every query the views, the server and the agents' query endpoint ran on LadybugDB returns the same results on PGlite (the existing view and traversal tests pass unchanged in meaning); the fact log reads and writes through the same storage interface on PGlite and PostgreSQL; pgvector serves the vector index locally; no LadybugDB or SQLite dependency remains in the shipped package; the clean-install walks pass on Linux x64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64.

## Left out
Cypher or SQL/PGQ as an agents' query language (agents write SQL until PGQ supports variable-length paths); performance tuning beyond keeping existing tests green.

title: Keep GitHub merge commits linked to their task.
description:
A GitHub PR was merged with the default merge-commit strategy while its branch commits and PR description carried a `Task:` line. The generated merge commit `abdd5ef262ddbfd7e69b1537b9a268689a12e47e` has no `Task:` line. Running `.shady2k/checks/check-commits.mjs` on the adapter export for `d76ead43740174dfd05884803d606ab6665aeab8..abdd5ef262ddbfd7e69b1537b9a268689a12e47e` exits 1 and reports `no task link`. The owner merged PR #16 before the full post-merge close-out audit found this.

## What should happen
Every commit, including a GitHub-generated merge commit, carries the task link required by `.shady2k/integration.md`, and the commit-link check passes for the accepted range.

## Done when
- The owner-approved remedy for the already-landed merge commit is recorded; do not rewrite shared `main` history without the owner's explicit direction.
- The normal PR merge path preserves or supplies the exact `Task: <id>` line on any merge commit, or otherwise prevents such a commit from landing under the existing policy.
- A regression check covers the merge-commit case, and `node .shady2k/checks/check-commits.mjs` passes for the reconciled range containing PR #16.

This is an integration/check-workflow defect, not a product finding; it blocks stage `madarch-24sy.3` close-out until the link is reconciled. No finding budget is charged.

title: Graph queries use PostgreSQL recursive CTEs
description:
## Done when
The graph query engine is asynchronous and uses PostgreSQL `WITH RECURSIVE` in local PGlite and server PostgreSQL. All existing children, views, context, collapsed/refined relations, dependents, dependencies, per-hop bitemporal/state filters, shortest-chain results, source unions and error behavior pass their focused tests with unchanged meaning. No Cypher query engine is used by graph, view, render or agent-query paths.

title: Add an asynchronous graph-query port with fair snapshots
description:
## Outcome
Add an asynchronous `AsyncQueryEngine` beside the existing synchronous `QueryEngine` as the expand step of a wide refactor. Add a query-only `QuerySnapshot` and an async compatibility adapter over the existing Ladybug engine. Keep all existing callers on the synchronous port in this task; later tasks migrate them in batches and remove the old port last. The compatibility adapter is only for Ladybug and must not be used to disguise PGlite's asynchronous API.

## Done when
The async port returns promises from `children`, `view`, `dependents`, `dependencies`, `rebuild`, `update` and `close`, and exposes `withSnapshot(work)` with query-only methods. One multi-query snapshot sees one graph revision. The admission gate is fair and writer-preferential: after an update queues, later snapshots cannot pass it, and queued writers run in order. A test pauses a snapshot, queues an update and then a later snapshot; after releasing the first snapshot, the update completes before the later snapshot starts. Update, rebuild and close wait without deadlock; close rejects new work. The Ladybug adapter returns the same query results and domain errors as the old port. Existing synchronous callers and tests still pass unchanged. `bun run check` and the focused query-engine and snapshot tests pass.

title: Implement the shared asynchronous PostgreSQL graph-query engine
description:
## Outcome
Implement the asynchronous SQL graph-query engine with one shared query database per local product data folder and the shared server PostgreSQL database. Store source provenance in a column and scope each graph's queries to its source set, so cross-source contract relations join in one SQL query. Keep the existing per-source HistoryStore databases from `.3.1` unchanged.

## Done when
- The SQL engine implements the async query and snapshot contract for PGlite and server PostgreSQL, using one PostgreSQL schema and query dialect; transitive traversal uses `WITH RECURSIVE`.
- Existing graph-query results and domain errors retain their meaning for children, views, context, collapsed/refined relations, dependents, dependencies, valid/known/state filters, shortest chains, source unions and rebuilds.
- A graph containing sources A and B resolves a cross-source relation in one SQL query; a graph scoped to A does not see B; existing duplicate-id rejection is preserved.
- Rebuild from full bitemporal history and incremental source updates give the same answers, including at earlier valid and known times. Updates affect only the changed source's rows.
- The local data folder owns one shared query database, not one query database per source; source histories remain isolated as before.
- One `withSnapshot` callback sees one revision. PGlite snapshot/write admission is shared and writer-fair; PostgreSQL snapshots use read-only repeatable-read transactions. Closing one graph scope never closes the shared database connection.
- Domain `QueryError` values remain structured results; unexpected SQL/connection errors reject the async operation.
- Focused query, graph, view, server and history-source tests plus `bun run check` pass.

## Out of scope
Migrating production callers to the new port and removing the synchronous/Ladybug path; later leaves do that after this engine works.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The shared owner preserves `.4.1` writer-preferential admission on both backends: PGlite serializes complete snapshots and writes on its one connection; PostgreSQL may overlap read-only repeatable-read snapshots, but active snapshots drain before queued writes and later snapshots cannot pass queued writers.
- [ ] Each rebuild and update is an atomic source-scoped transaction; failures roll back without exposing a partial projection, and rows for other sources remain unchanged.
- [ ] A borrowed engine scope can close without closing the shared owner or sibling scopes; owner close rejects new work, drains active operations and closes the connection exactly once. Cross-facade calls from inside `withSnapshot` reject, and the supplied reader expires after the callback.
- [ ] The PostgreSQL adapter is exercised against a real PostgreSQL fixture for snapshot, write and lifecycle behavior, in addition to the PGlite suite.

title: The legacy Ladybug adapter can choose a non-lexicographic chain for equal shortest dependency paths.
description:
The legacy Ladybug graph-query path may choose the wrong equal-length dependency route when node traversal order differs from relation-ID order. Its Cypher `SHORTEST` query returns one path before the adapter compares relation-ID chains, so the adapter cannot always select the code-point least chain. The SQL query engine added in `.4.2` has a regression test for this contract, but production callers remain on the Ladybug path until later migration work.

## Done when
- If the stage removes Ladybug from all graph-query callers, its migration keeps the SQL code-point tie-break regression test and no production graph-query route uses the legacy adapter.
- If Ladybug remains in use, a reversed-order equal-shortest-path fixture proves the legacy adapter returns the code-point least relation-ID chain for both dependencies and dependents.

## Disprove
Run the reversed-order fixture against the current Ladybug adapter. If it always returns the code-point least chain, this finding is not reproduced.

## Left out
Changing the SQL engine, changing the code-point tie contract, or migrating production callers independently of the planned graph-query stage.

## Decision needed
The standalone finding budget is already 7/7, so this is deferred until 2026-10-22. Recommend keeping it deferred while the planned graph-query migration removes the Ladybug path; if that path remains, decide whether to displace planned work and raise the finding budget.

title: Move production graph, render, and model-check queries to the asynchronous SQL engine.
description:
## Problem
The SQL query database and asynchronous query port are on main (base `232c36a0`), but production graph serving and model rendering still construct the synchronous Ladybug engine. The SQL migration is not complete until those callers use the shared SQL projection and await its lifecycle.

## Solution
Migrate the production graph service, HTTP query routes, rendering, and model-check view preparation to `AsyncQueryDatabase` and `AsyncQueryEngine`. Use one shared owner for each server data folder, source-scoped facades, a single rebuild from HistoryStore assertions, and incremental store reports. Multi-query views and renders must use `withSnapshot`; close graph facades and the database owner on shutdown. Keep the current per-source HistoryStore topology and the public response/rendering contracts.

## Done when
- Production graph-serving, rendering, and model-check paths no longer construct or call the synchronous Ladybug engine.
- A server graph rebuilds its scoped SQL projection from history, tracks successful stores, clears a removed source, and closes its borrowed facade and shared owner exactly once.
- Multi-query view/render requests use one snapshot; an overlapping store cannot produce a mixed-revision response.
- Existing graph, HTTP, render, and model-check outputs and error/refusal shapes remain unchanged, with regression tests for lifecycle, source scope, and snapshot overlap.
- `bun run check` and all changed focused suites pass; the PostgreSQL adapter's existing integration checks remain green.

## Out of scope
Removing the Ladybug adapter and package/build/install dependencies, changing the history-store layout or legacy `.sqlite` refusal, adding vector providers, publishing, and clean-install walks. Those follow in separate leaves.

title: Retire LadybugDB, the local SQLite store, and native OpenSSL installation paths.
description:
## Problem
The production graph, rendering and model-check paths now use the asynchronous SQL query database, but the synchronous Ladybug engine, its compatibility bridge, and its native package remain. The native package brings platform addons and an OpenSSL runtime dependency into installs and compiled binaries. The local SQLite HistoryStore has already been replaced by PGlite; only a deliberate refusal of old `.sqlite` files remains for data safety.

## Solution
Contract the staged migration: remove the synchronous query port and Ladybug adapters once all remaining tests use the asynchronous SQL engine; remove Ladybug native dependencies and trusted-install hooks from the package and lockfile; remove native-addon/OpenSSL-specific logic from binary/release/install paths; update the live architecture model and current implementation docs. Keep historical decisions intact, preserve the legacy `.sqlite` refusal, and keep local PGlite plus the injected server PostgreSQL owner.

## Done when
- Production code, public exports, and tests no longer import or instantiate LadybugDB or the synchronous `QueryEngine`; SQL coverage uses fixed expected outcomes and tests the async PGlite/PostgreSQL interfaces without a Ladybug oracle.
- `package.json` and `bun.lock` contain no Ladybug packages or native-addon trust/install path. The release binary and installer scripts contain no Ladybug/OpenSSL requirement; a compiled local smoke opens and exercises the PGlite-backed query path without a system OpenSSL library.
- No SQLite HistoryStore implementation, SQLite/SQLite-vector runtime dependency, or `bun:sqlite` use remains. The explicit legacy `.sqlite` refusal and its rebuild/resend guidance remain tested.
- The live architecture model and implementation docs describe local PGlite and injected server PostgreSQL accurately; historical decision records remain historical.
- `bun run check`, the focused query/server/render/model-check suites, and the binary smoke pass. PostgreSQL integration is run when `MADARCH_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is configured and otherwise recorded as skipped.

## Out of scope
Clean-install walks on Linux, macOS and Windows (separate install-stage leaves), provider/model work, publishing, and accepting or closing tasks/stages.

title: The backlog adapter carries command-run records so repeated checks honor prior bounds.
description:
A fresh `node .shady2k/adapter.mjs backlog` export currently keeps only comments starting with `[shady2k-time`, while `runs.mjs exec` writes `<!-- shady2k-exec v1 -->` comments and reads prior durations from the adapter export. On 2026-10-15, the `.7` task received execution records for `bun run check` (1 s), `bun test test/server-http.test.ts` (110 s), and `bun test test/server-views.test.ts` (46 s), but a fresh adapter export still omitted all of them. This makes a later run see no previous duration and use a first-run/default bound instead of the longest recorded duration.

## Done when
- A fresh normalized adapter export includes raw `shady2k-exec v1` comments along with existing `shady2k-time` comments.
- A repeated `runs.mjs exec` invocation with the exact same argv uses the longest completed recorded duration as its bound, not the first-run default.
- Ordinary comments do not become run records.

## Disproved by
A posted execution record is missing from the fresh export, or a repeat of the same command still chooses the first-run/default bound.

## Left out
No change to command behavior, test timeout values, or the `shady2k-exec` record format. Discovered while recording the `.7` repair; it is separate from that startup-fixture change.

title: Make the reference system's views readable
description:
Decided by the owner on 2026-09-25 after looking at the merged views of madarch-mk5. Rendered by GitHub's own Mermaid renderer in a 1150 px column (a wide screen), 5 of the 8 pages show arrow labels under 12 px (the landscape 7.8 px, storefront 8.3 px, fulfilment 9.6 px, platform 11.7 px, ordering 11.9 px) and 7 of 8 have labels overlapping each other or a box. Causes: merged labels of up to 103 characters widen the diagrams; a topic's consumer is drawn as an arrow into the broker, named for what it does, so it reads as sending; the broker gathers every arrow; in an element's own view the general relation is drawn from the frame instead of its refinement from the module that does it; merged labels mix publishing and consuming in id order.

## Done when
On every page of the reference system rendered by GitHub's Mermaid in a 1150 px column, arrow labels
are at least 12 px and no label overlaps another label or a box (measured by rendering every page
and recorded with the numbers); every arrow carries its row number and every relation behind it is
in that row of the table under its diagram; a topic's publishers and subscribers are marked
(action: send | receive), their arrows drawn from the initiator, dashed, and entered by role; in an
element's own view its module's refinement is drawn, not the general relation from its frame;
likec4 validate and the Mermaid parse still pass.
(Rewritten 2026-09-27 by the owner's decisions: arrows from the initiator instead of from the broker
(madarch-48x.1), and numbered arrows instead of word labels after measurement.)

## Left out
Direct producer-to-consumer arrows through a topic (a derived relation, a later decision); views per environment or state; the server.
close_reason: Criterion met on 6c8f709 (the rewritten Done when): all 8 pages 13.1 px or more with no overlaps, numbered arrows with every relation in the table, publishers and subscribers marked and dashed, the module's refinement drawn, likec4 validate and the Mermaid parse pass. Stage madarch-48x.2 accepted; PR #2 merged by the owner.

title: Decide how the model marks a topic's or queue's consumer
description:
A decision the owner holds (asked 2026-09-25). In the format, publishing to and consuming from a topic are written alike (a relation from the service to the broker naming the topic interface); only the relation's name tells them apart, so a renderer cannot draw an event from the broker to its consumer.

Options: (1) an optional relation field consumes: true for a consumer of a topic or queue interface (a small, explicit format addition; relations without it unchanged); (2) no format change: event relations drawn dashed and labelled with the topic, arrow direction unchanged; (3) inferring from the name: fragile, not recommended.

Recommendation: (1).

Affects: the task that draws events from the broker to the consumer. Meanwhile the labels and the refinement tasks proceed.
close_reason: Owner decided 2026-09-27: an optional relation field action: send | receive on relations through a topic:: or queue:: interface (Codex's proposal, after AsyncAPI 3). Arrows stay drawn from the initiator (from -> to, as every other arrow), labelled by role: 'publishes <topic>' or 'subscribes to <topic>', dashed; no reversed arrows (owner, citing C4: the initiator's arrow).

title: Mark a topic's or queue's publishers and subscribers, and label their arrows by role
description:
Decided by the owner on 2026-09-27 (madarch-48x.1). A relation through a topic:: or queue:: interface may carry action: send | receive. from/to stays the dependency edge; the arrow is drawn from the initiator as every other arrow, dashed, labelled 'publishes <topic>' (send) or 'subscribes to <topic>' (receive), in Mermaid and LikeC4; the relation's name goes in the arrow table. A topic or queue relation without action loads with a warning and is drawn as today; action on any other relation is an error naming its YAML line. transfers.direction stays as written (a received event is normally reverse); no consistency check. The reference model marks every publisher and subscriber. Queries and dependencies unchanged; topic-impact queries stay out.

## Done when
intended-model and compiled-model specs and schemas carry action with the rules above; views draw event arrows by role in both formats; every topic relation of the reference model has its action; bun run schemas and bun run views reproduce the committed files; related tests pass.

title: Create and rename products through the skill set's pinned product-repository program, keeping madarch new as its thin wrapper
description:
Decision 0019 (owner, 2026-10-09): the product repository's lifecycle (layout, workspace.yaml schema, create, rename, bootstrap) is a program the shady2k-skills set ships. madarch-rtr builds madarch's own draft creation and `madarch new` first, as the reference the set ports; once the set publishes its program, madarch pins that release, makes `madarch new` (and any `madarch rename`) a thin wrapper over it, removes its own creation code, and keeps its manifest reader with consumer tests against the set's fixtures and hand-written folders.

title: The product's knowledge keeps a changelog of what changed in the understanding of the product, and answers given in the wiki's chat are filed back as pages
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-14 ~23:55 MSK, after comparing madarch with Google Code Wiki, DeepWiki and Hermes code-wiki, Wiki Architect, the LLM Wiki Schema and product-architect. The owner doubted whether madarch is needed over code-only wikis; the agreed position: keep the core (intent linked to code across repositories, checked) and fix the value a person gets in the first minutes. Taken up after the standalone milestone's wiki-usable work, not into the current slice.

An append-only log says what was learned or changed about the product and when (a decision taken, a requirement changed, a claim corrected), readable as 'what changed this week'. A good answer the wiki's agent gave in chat can be filed into the wiki as a page or a correction, with its sources, so knowledge accumulates instead of being re-derived per question (see madarch-cuu). Reference: the LLM Wiki Schema's log.md and query-to-page.

Would show it is worth it: a reader back from a week away catches up from the log alone.
Left out: chat history as such.

This widens the milestone idea-to-wiki by a scope decision recorded in the charter: the exclusions "the team: bootstrap of a cloned product, several people on one product" and "code repositories beyond the first" no longer hold for the pieces below. Nothing planned is displaced; outcomes 2-5 (madarch-fe1, madarch-0uc, madarch-ls3, madarch-mni) keep their order after it. madarch-mni overlaps: only what this needs is taken from it; the naming conversation stays with the skills (leave it there).

The bundled product-repository program (vendor/shady2k-skills/0.94.0) already exports rename, remote, bootstrap, repo add and where. The madarch command (src/product/cli.ts, scripts/madarch.ts) exposes only new, serve and list. This feature exposes the lifecycle as thin wrappers over the program, with the same refusals and exit codes as the existing commands, and gives engineers one guide page.

## Work
- madarch rename <name> [--product <folder>]
- madarch remote <url> [--product <folder>]
- madarch repo add <name> <url> [--branch <b>] [--product <folder>] (enters the repository in the manifest, then clones it into repos/<name> through bootstrap; an already-present checkout is left alone and reported)
- madarch bootstrap [--product <folder>]
- madarch clone <url> [--home <folder>]: git clone of a product repository into the products home, then bootstrap, then print the folder and how to open its wiki; this is how a second engineer joins
- the default product folder is the current folder's product (the program's where), so the commands work when run inside a product
- the products home stays ~/madarch/products, moved by MADARCH_HOME or --home; tests never write into the real home
- the capability spec (docs/system/capabilities/product-repository.md) and a change record as the documents gate requires
- the engineer's guide: docs/guides/start-a-product.md, with a pointer from README.md; every command copy-pasteable, what each prints, and running setup-shady2k-skills in the product as the product-repository case

## Left out
The naming conversation of outcome 5 (madarch-mni keeps it; the draft is renamed into an example name at most); several people on one product beyond the first clone; remote transport beyond git; agents through MCP or an API (madarch-yhy); work launched from the wiki.

## DONE WHEN
The acceptance walk, in a scratch home: madarch new; rename to an example name; repo add two real small public repositories; remote to a local bare repository standing in for GitHub; push; then madarch clone of that remote into a second scratch home as the second engineer: both repositories appear under repos/, the wiki serves, and a file saved under docs/ shows on its page. title: Make the five lifecycle commands thin wrappers over the pinned program, with their tests
description:
The madarch command gains the five subcommands as thin wrappers over the bundled pinned program's exports (renameProduct, addRemote, bootstrapProduct, addCodeRepository, whereAmI; vendor/shady2k-skills/0.94.0), with src/product/program.ts extended to name them and product.d.mts extended (the declarations are written in this repository, never in the vendored file) with the shapes as the program's own documentation and self-test give them.

Commands and contracts (parent madarch-525o and its brief):
- madarch rename <name> [--product <folder>]: renames the draft's folder in place, keeps the internal id; refuses a name that cannot be used with exit 2 in the program's words.
- madarch remote <url> [--product <folder>]: sets (or replaces) the git remote the program manages.
- madarch repo add <name> <url> [--branch <b>] [--product <folder>]: enters the repository in the manifest, then clones it into repos/<name> through the program's bootstrap; an already-present checkout is left alone and reported as the program reports it.
- madarch bootstrap [--product <folder>]: clones what the manifest declares.
- madarch clone <url> [--home <folder>]: git clone of a product repository into the products home, then bootstrap, then print the product's folder, its id and how to open its wiki; this is how a second engineer joins.
- The default product folder is the program's where: the current folder's product when no --product is given, so the commands work when run inside a product.
- Exit codes and refusal style match the existing commands: 2 for an argument, a product folder, a manifest or a home that cannot be used; 1 when a step (git) failed; errors name what is wrong, one message per error, on standard error; stdout prints facts one per line.
- The products home stays ~/madarch/products, moved by MADARCH_HOME or --home where the command takes it; tests never write into the real home (the scratch-home helpers).
- help and usage text cover the new subcommands.

TDD: watch a behaviour test fail for the intended reason, then the least code. Tests beside the existing ones (test/product-cli.test.ts and neighbours; the scratch-home helpers), through the CLI's main() as the existing tests do where that reaches the behaviour; git-invoking steps use the project's test git conventions (test/git-env.ts).
Doubled: the module's own decisions (which url/name to hand the program, which streams) are madarch's; the lifecycle calls are the program's only.

Check: bun run check; MADARCH_SKIP_PERF=1 bun test; the new tests iterated alone.
close_reason: done

title: A person working in an existing code checkout starts a madarch product around it and keeps working where they are
description:
Agreed with the owner on 2026-10-13. A person runs an agent (Codex, Claude Code) in their own code repository, in a folder of their choosing, decides to manage the product with madarch, and ends with a product repository under the products home that holds the docs, the model and the tracker, with their checkout as one of its code repositories, nothing moved unless they choose it.

What the owner decided:
- The product repository is separate (~/madarch/products/<name>); code repositories are entered in workspace.yaml and live under its repos/ (untracked).
- `madarch repo add` run for a checkout that already exists on the machine offers three ways: link to it (the default: a symlink, or a directory junction on Windows, which needs no administrator rights), move it into repos/ (branches, uncommitted work and stash kept), or clone afresh. A machine where neither link can be made says so plainly and offers moving or cloning.
- Nothing of madarch is ever written into the code repository (owner: "В репозитории с кодом не должно быть частей madarch"). A checkout outside a product finds its product by scanning the products home for a repos/ entry that links to it; madarch, the wiki and describe-repository read a linked checkout as a checkout and never clone over it.
- The product repository explains itself to the person: its README says what the product repository is, what docs/, model/ and repos/ hold, and that one madarch command builds the whole workspace (clones or links every declared repository, connects the tracker); there is no Makefile — the madarch command works the same on Windows (owner: «если у нас будет cli, то нам никакой make файл не нужен»).
- The person is told to restart their agent from the product folder, where the docs, the tracker and the code are all in reach; a command such as `madarch work <name>` may open that place (owner: "Можешь быть даже сделать команду типа madarch work <имя>").
- The skill set's side (its setup hints once at madarch in a project with no product repository; its product detection follows the link) is filed in the set's own tracker.

## DONE WHEN
From a code checkout in any folder (a throwaway git repository made for the walk, with a local branch, uncommitted work and a stash), one guided path ends with ~/madarch/products/<name> whose wiki serves that code repository through a link, the checkout still in place with its branch and uncommitted work untouched, no file added to it, `madarch list` naming the product, the agent restarted from the product folder seeing docs and tracker, and one madarch command on a fresh clone of the product reproducing the workspace; the same walk on Windows with a junction.

## Left out
The tracker store off the branches (madarch-tjum); multi-machine sync of the link (links are per machine by design); importing the code repository's own history into the product.
notes: Owner Addendum 7 follow-on: when this feature ships the working repository-connect/clone command(s), update the localized empty/no-manifest home guide to include those newly available steps. Do not suggest those commands in the guide before they work.

title: Connect an explicit checkout by link, move or clone through madarch repo add
description:
Implement `madarch repo add` support for connecting an explicitly selected checkout to an existing product. The command accepts the repository name and remote URL, plus `--source <path>` for a local checkout and `--mode link|move|clone` for the connection choice. No local checkout is searched for implicitly. If a local source is supplied interactively, ask the person how to connect it and default to link. In non-interactive runs, require `--mode`; with URL only, clone without searching.

## DONE WHEN
- `madarch repo add <name> <url> --source <path>` links the selected Git top level by default (symlink, or a directory junction on Windows), without writing to the code checkout.
- `--mode move` relocates the checkout under the product's `repos/` and preserves its local branch, uncommitted work and stash.
- `--mode clone` clones the declared URL under `repos/`. A URL without `--source` never triggers a search.
- An interactive local-source run asks link/move/clone, with link as default. A non-interactive local-source run without `--mode` refuses and names the required flag. Invalid combinations are refused, not silently ignored.
- Failures name the selected path or URL and leave the source unchanged unless the requested move completes. If a link cannot be made, the failure says plainly that the person can choose move or clone.
- Tests use temporary local Git repositories only, each with a local branch, uncommitted work and a stash; expected results come from this task. Unit tests cover the Windows junction branch. No test needs an outside checkout or network.

title: Stage 2: Start a product around the current checkout and show its code in the wiki
description:
The approved 0.1.1 brief adds `madarch init` around the current Git checkout, repository content in the wiki, state-aware getting-started guidance, and CLI usage/version behavior. Keep the checkout in place and use the existing `repo add` link operation.

## DONE WHEN
A person inside a Git checkout can run `madarch init` and get a committed product under the configured products home that links the checkout and serves/opens the wiki. Outside Git refuses with `madarch new`; an existing product/already-linked checkout is unchanged; no origin works and is explained; collision refuses clearly. `--port` and `--no-open` work. Tests use local temporary repositories and bare origins only.

## Left out
Changing the approved behavior, moving checkout contents, or adding engine-owned state.

title: Improve first-contact CLI help and first-run wiki guidance
description:
Fix the first-contact behavior reported from madarch 0.1.1.

## Done when
- `madarch` with no arguments, `madarch help`, `madarch --help`, and `madarch -h` print short grouped help to stdout and exit 0. It describes madarch, has Start (new, init), Work with a product (serve, list, repo add, rename, remote, clone, bootstrap, demo), Other (version, upgrade), and ends with `madarch <command> --help`. Each command has one plain-English line and top-level help has no flags.
- `<command> --help` and `-h` show command usage, flags each on one line, and an example, then exit 0. Unknown commands and bad flags name the problem on stderr, exit 2, suggest `madarch --help`, and do not print a usage wall.
- Remove user-facing `bun link` lines, retaining them only in developer docs if needed. Preserve `version: X` output.
- Empty-product wiki Getting started shows, in order: code path `cd <checkout> && madarch init` or `madarch repo add`; document path: run an agent with `setup-shady2k-skills` in product folder.
- Overview repository url, path, and state are visually separated at 1400 and 390 px; names do not break mid-word.
- Add CLI help/exit-code/per-command and app tests. Read real-server browser screenshots at both widths.
- Before push, build binary with `bun scripts/build-binary.ts --version 0.0.1 --os linux --arch x64 --out <scratch>`.


## Owner addition (2026-10-16)
- No-argument invocation identifies its context first: unlinked Git checkout says `This folder is a git repository. To start a product around it: madarch init`; product folder says `This is the product <name>. Open its wiki: madarch serve. To write its documents, run an agent (e.g. Claude Code) here and ask for setup-shady2k-skills.`; elsewhere says `Start a new product: madarch new — or cd into your code repository and run madarch init`. Always state products live in `~/madarch/products`, or `MADARCH_HOME`. Then show the short command list.
- After `new` and `init`, print Next steps with product folder, `cd <folder> && madarch serve`, and running an agent in that folder with setup-shady2k-skills. `init` says code stays where it is.
- install.sh and install.ps1 end by printing the same two start commands.
- Test all no-argument contexts (temporary Git checkout, product, elsewhere), and next steps for creation. Preserve `version: X`.


## Owner addition 2 (2026-10-16)
Headless/remote serving and bind host are in scope. When no desktop/opener exists, or an SSH session is detected (`SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY`, or Linux without `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`), do not attempt browser opening and print `Wiki: http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Over SSH add: `This machine is remote. On your computer run: ssh -L <port>:127.0.0.1:<port> <user>@<host> then open http://localhost:<port>`; fill user and host from env when available and use `<host>` otherwise. A failing opener prints the same calm Wiki line plus its reason, not an error. Add `--host <address>` to serve/new/init/demo; default remains 127.0.0.1 (decision 0012). For non-loopback host, print a one-line warning that the wiki is reachable from the network without a password. Test no opener, SSH env, opener failure, and --host.


## Owner addition 3 — acceptance bar
Every command output must tell a newcomer what happened, where things are, how to open wiki from their location, and next step, following Jupyter-style output. For `init` over SSH, target exact shape from the brief: success lines for created product and connected repository; running wiki URL and Ctrl+C; SSH tunnel command using local port, remote server address, SSH user and host; next steps for agent document setup and reopening wiki. Use the same shape for `new`, `serve`, `demo`, and `clone`, as applicable. Show home paths with `~`. Keep machine-readable facts (`folder`, `id`, `url`, etc.) behind `--json`, and update existing tests/scripts parsing them, including `scripts/clean-homebrew-walk.sh`, release smoke steps and `test/*`. Final report must include exact terminal output of new, init local, init with SSH_CONNECTION, and serve.


## Owner addition 4
- Overview repo state must distinguish actual linked symlink, cloned, moved, and missing state; translate labels to English and Russian; test every state.
- Do not require shady2k-skills. Product documents are Markdown in the product docs/ folder and can be written by hand or with any agent; optional wording: “or let an agent set them up with the shady2k-skills set”. Apply to both locales, CLI next steps and inside-product hint.

title: Generate a wiki with diagrams from a repository's model
description:
Owner 2026-09-29: Markdown documents in a repository are hard to read; madarch generates documentation with diagrams, not only diagrams. One shared page-data layer built from the compiled model (home, domains, elements, interfaces, zones, data categories, cross-linked), and two engine adapters, Zensical and Starlight, chosen by MADARCH_WIKI_ENGINE (default zensical) or --engine. Command: bun scripts/wiki.ts <repo> --out <dir>; the outcome-4 server reuses it. The throwaway prototypes of madarch-ti6.3 are the reference; the code is written anew with tests.

## DONE WHEN
the reference system's and nocx's wikis build on both engines from the model alone; on their pages the interactive LikeC4 diagram opens with element details and drill-down, and the Mermaid diagram renders; the built sites have no broken links.

title: The wiki's Starlight engine fails to build when the wiki cache root is the default under the owner's home folder
description:
Found 2026-10-02 standing both engines' wikis of the reference system up for example.

What a person does: builds a wiki with the Starlight engine and no MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE set, so the cache root is the default under the home folder (XDG ~/.cache/madarch/wiki).

What happens: the build exits 1 with the engine's output: astro/vite refuses with "No cached compile metadata found" for @astrojs/starlight/dist/components/Page.astro, and the main-module id it names is mangled — the project root joined onto the cache's absolute path with its leading slash dropped (source/home/dev/.cache/madarch/wiki/template-…/node_modules/…). The same happens under node 24 directly, so it is not the bun runtime.

What should happen: exit 0 with the built site's path (capability wiki, requirement result).

Measured on this machine (same template, same pages, only the named variable changed):
- project under /tmp, node_modules symlinked at the default cache under /home/dev/.cache: build fails;
- project under /tmp, node_modules symlinked at a cache under /tmp (MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE, as the tests move it): build passes, 90 pages;
- the same project, node_modules copied (not symlinked) from the failing /home/dev/.cache install: build passes, 82 pages.

So the trigger is the engine's symlinked node_modules (linkStarlightNodeModules in src/wiki/starlight.ts) resolving into the default cache location, likely a path mishandling in the pinned astro 7.3.5 / rolldown-vite. Untested: whether a project folder also under the home folder fails the same way.

Workaround while deferred: point MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE at a folder outside the home cache (the gated tests already do).

Disproved by: a Starlight build with the default cache root succeeding on a machine with the pinned toolchain, or the trigger shown to be a machine-specific install rather than the symlink-to-default-cache path.

## Done when
- a real Starlight build with the default cache root (no MADARCH_WIKI_CACHE) succeeds on a clean user account, or the writer stops symlinking node_modules from a cache the engine cannot resolve through, naming what replaced it;
- the pinned template's bun.lock stays reproducible: two builds of the same repository still give byte-identical source trees.

title: Keep the query engine's buffer pool from filling under thousands of updates without a rebuild
description:
Found 2026-09-30 by the rework worker of madarch-ti6.2 (change server-views), measured with LadybugDB 0.20.4 under Bun 1.4.2, every query result closed.

## What was measured
- The engine's update path (update -> removeRelation/closeEdge, inserts) grows RSS about 115 KB per update call; with no reads in the loop and a rebuild every 500 calls, the 256 MiB buffer pool is exhausted ('Buffer manager exception: Unable to allocate memory! The buffer pool is full and no memory could be freed') after 5 032 updates and 10 rebuilds. At 2 000 calls RSS climbs linearly from 126 to 356 MB.
- Closing results does not change it (169 157 against 172 506 bytes per call, within noise); reads amplify it through statement churn but do not cause it.
- The read path is bounded: 24 000 dependents and view calls plateau near 160 MB.
- The engine opens new Database(':memory:', 256 MiB, false, false, 4 GiB), so autoCheckpoint stays at its default; the mechanism (WAL, version pages, allocator retention) is not yet known.

## Why it matters, and why not now
The MVP's server updates a graph's engine once per model sent and rebuilds it at start, so thousands of updates between restarts are far off; a server receiving models from CI or webhooks (live-graph) would reach it within days.

## Done when
The cause is found (a checkpoint, a periodic rebuild from the history, or a LadybugDB defect reported with a reproduction), and a test of at least 10 000 updates with rebuilds, yielding between batches, stays under a stated memory bound, skipped with the performance tests.

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@vm-agents:feature/registry-integrity
comments.text:
Deferred out of live-graph's outcome 1 by the owner, 2026-10-07 ("Я предлагаю этим заняться позже, это нас не блокирует" / "Убери это требование"). Revisit before outcome 3 (madarch-tah) starts: a server fed by CI reaches the bound within days.

Where it stood (run madarch-l19, worker l19-3-mem, 2026-10-02): growth is linear on the update path, ~10.3 MB per 250 updates (137 -> 294 MB over 4000, heading past the 400 MB bound); a disk-backed engine did not help; a smaller buffer pool makes LadybugDB fail. A probe rebuilding the engine from the history every 1000 updates plateaus at 185-192 MB with identical answers: the retained memory is the engine's, not the data's. Proposed mechanism, not yet decided: rebuild the engine from the history when growth exceeds a budget (e.g. +64 MB over its build). Open: the cause inside LadybugDB (not reported upstream); rebuild cost and its peak on a large model (measured only on a one-element model). The measured test and the probe are uncommitted in the worktree ~/.herdr/worktrees/madarch/w-l19-3-memory (test/query-engine-update-memory.test.ts, probe-rebuild-cycle.ts).

## Do this first
Present the preflight below to the owner again (in Russian, briefly) and ask for acceptance as a whole or changes by item; on acceptance run take-task on this task. The owner declined to start today only because of the 2-3 h estimate.

## Decisions (proposed in the preflight, NOT yet accepted by the owner)
1. Evidence level: records (no CI); records are trusted, not verified; say so in the integration.
2. Change format: docs/changes/<id>/change.md per the skills' template, plus full proposed capability files docs/changes/<id>/capabilities/<name>.md; the adapter computes deltas by comparing them with the current capability at the target revision (no hand-written deltas). 3. Catalogue: docs/system/index.md ('no coverage yet') and an empty capabilities/ directory; no invented sample capability (departure from documents.md's seed advice, justified by 'no empty scaffolds' and 'first change may add against an absent baseline').
4. Enforcement in the commit-msg hook: every commit -> product phase; a commit touching product code (outside docs/, .shady2k/, .beads/, .githooks/, root *.md) -> its linked task must belong to a change passing the feature phase; a commit touching docs/system/capabilities/ -> close phase; stage acceptance -> acceptance phase run by take-task as a command.
5. Policy: behavior/no-behavior owe static, test, mutation, review; supporting owes review plus the tooling's own tests; commands for static/test arrive with the first code (foundation feature madarch-ozp).
6. requireApproval: true for behavior changes; approval is one sentence in the preflight, recorded as the owner's words; changeDigest per documents.md.
7. Evidence storage: tracker comments on the change's tasks, first line 'check: {id,status,reference}' or 'approval: {changeDigest,reference}'.
8. Exemptions: none needed (no open task has code); this task is a supporting change.
9. Write both sentences into the integration: local hooks are feedback, not a boundary (--no-verify bypasses them); a refusal is owed work whoever could walk past it.
Estimate: 2-3 h agent work (a guess: no run history). Run mode: inline in the owner's session. Review: same-model independent reviewer, disclosed (Codex MCP was not connected).

description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-09: the wiki's agent improves itself. Each product repository already holds `skills/`, the team's own skills for that product, which is the natural first place.

Three levels, rising in risk: (1) the product's own skills: the agent sees it is corrected the same way again and again and proposes a change to a skill in `skills/`; (2) the shared skill set, another repository, reached the way a skills issue is filed today; (3) madarch's own code, as a feature run. At every level the change goes through the same path: a tracked task, a pull request, a replay on recorded past cases showing it does better and breaks nothing, and the owner's acceptance. Without that measure it is drift, not evolution.

Related: the owner's lifemodel project changes its own code by commits with an automatic revert; see the idea on lifemodel as the first outside agent.

Would show it is worth it: corrections of one kind stop recurring after the agent's own change to a product skill, measured on the replay.
Left out: changes to another repository without its own review and acceptance.

title: A CI or developer-machine runner uploads facts to the server API when it has no repository access
description:
Owner decision (2026-10-12 ~22:40 MSK, /tmp/madarch-run-iuc/note-storage-boundary.md, decision 0023): code itself never leaves its network. A runner in CI or on a developer machine (feature 0007's ingest surface) uploads imported facts to the server API when the server has no repository access; each fact carries its evidence (source system, ref or commit, record id) and is READ-ONLY in the wiki (authored entities stay writable, provenance 0005).

## DONE WHEN (when opened)
A runner without git access to the product repositories uploads facts through the server API with evidence attached; the server stores them in its fact log with provenance; an uploaded fact renders read-only in the wiki with its evidence named; an upload without evidence is refused naming the missing field; review converged.

title: Take lifemodel as the first outside agent of agent-access: working with the wiki over MCP, and developing the product through its process
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-09: take lifemodel, the owner's own proactive agent project (it acts when pressure builds rather than when polled, changes its own code by commits with an automatic revert, and runs tasks through prime-agent), as an agent working with the product in madarch.

Two roles, kept apart: (1) a conversational agent in the wiki: decision 0017 already lets a person's own agent connect through MCP or the API by the same checked write path, so madarch depends on nothing of lifemodel's and keeps its own server agent for people without one; (2) a developer of the product: lifemodel changes itself without a human step, but madarch's or a product's code only by that repository's process (tracked task, checks, pull request, the owner's acceptance).

Where they meet: the agent-access milestone (MCP and API, madarch-yhy) could take lifemodel as its first outside agent and be accepted on its real work with the wiki, not a synthetic client. Its proactivity fits the wiki: noticing open questions, stale documents and unanswered comments.

Would show it is worth it: when agent-access is chartered, lifemodel has passed its own instance-1 milestone and can hold a session against madarch's MCP.
Left out: making madarch's built-in agent lifemodel.

title: Publish a product release over two sources, joined at the contract boundary
description:
Outcome 2 of live-graph (charter docs/milestones/live-graph.md). product.yaml names the product's member sources and the corpus custody (today the single repository's docs/product/, movable later without changing identity or URLs); a release is published atomically from one manifest pinning every artifact by digest — never synthesized from the latest received state — and publishing validates that every referenced artifact exists and is intact; the landscape joins sources at the contract boundary only; an id clash across sources is reported naming both sources, never merged last-writer-wins; a thin portal builds from a pinned release (shared navigation, product overview, per-source namespaces). Full graph merging beyond the contract boundary stays out.

## DONE WHEN
with the real repository as one source and a synthetic second source: a release manifest pins both sources' artifacts by digest; publishing validates and records atomically; an id clash at the contract boundary refuses the release naming both sources; the portal builds from the pinned release; changing one source and publishing a new release rebuilds the portal without touching the other.

Replanned against decision 0016 (docs/decisions/0016-product-knowledge-base-direction.md) once to-milestone has reworked the vision and milestones: the portal becomes the product portal and the corpus follows the versioned document contract. Owner decision 2026-10-08.

title: Update the GitHub Actions workflows for supported runtimes and runner images.
description:
This is CI/setup maintenance, not a feature finding. Main CI run 38662905562 and Product documents run 38662904068 passed but emitted GitHub runner annotations: `actions/checkout@v4` is forced from Node.js 20 to Node.js 24, and `ubuntu-latest` is scheduled to migrate to Ubuntu 26 beginning 2026-10-19. The workflows use supported action runtimes and a deliberate, validated runner selection for the Ubuntu 26 transition. CI, Product documents, and the relevant release workflow checks pass without the Node.js 20 or `ubuntu-latest` migration warnings.

## Not in scope
Changing product behavior, packaging policy, or publishing a release.

comments.text:
Decision / validation plan

- Update actions to their current Node 24 major lines: `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, and `actions/download-artifact@v8`. Official action releases and manifests: checkout v7.0.1 / node24 (https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v7.0.1, https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/v7/action.yml); setup-node v7.1.0 / node24 (https://github.com/actions/setup-node/releases/tag/v7.1.0, https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/v7/action.yml); upload-artifact v7.0.2 / node24 (https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v7.0.2, https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/v7/action.yml); download-artifact v8.0.2 / node24 (https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v8.0.2, https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/v8/action.yml).
- Pin Ubuntu x64 jobs to `ubuntu-24.04`, preserving `ubuntu-24.04-arm` and existing macOS labels. GitHub’s migration issue says the `ubuntu-latest` move to 26.04 starts 2026-10-19 (https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14748); explicit 24.04 preserves the current tested image and avoids an automatic change. This task does not migrate to 26.04.
- Remove `.github/workflows/**` from CI’s `paths-ignore`; otherwise this workflow-only task would skip the root CI run needed to validate its own changes.
- Validate release preparation on PRs that change `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Split read-only packaging from the final tag-only `gh release create` job. Give `contents:write` only to the publish job, conditioned on a `push` of a `v*` tag; PR build/package uses `v0.0.0`. Preserve the tag release’s asset set and publishing behavior. No PR can publish and no release is triggered.
- Scenarios: workflow-only branch pushes run CI and Product documents; the release-validation PR builds/tests all four binary targets and packages artifacts; the publish job is skipped; a `v*` tag still publishes the same prepared release assets.

Official runner and trigger references: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners#standard-github-hosted-runners-for-public-repositories ; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request .

title: Work with the wiki through an agent in a chat beside each page: answer questions and comments, create and edit entities
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-09, discussing the wiki. Decision 0017 already chose it ("a chat beside every page"); the idea-to-wiki charter keeps it out of that milestone, and nothing in the tracker carried it until now.

Beside each page, a person writes what they want and an agent works with them on the wiki: answers questions about the product, answers comments, creates documents and other entities, edits the page. It knows the page and the graph around it, writes through the same checked path, each change its own commit so undoing it is one action, and waits for no confirmation. The agent runs on the madarch server with the skill set's behaviour; a person's own agent connects through MCP or the API instead (see the idea on lifemodel as the first outside agent).

Would show it is worth it: in the milestone walk the owner keeps asking an agent outside the wiki to do what the page in front of them should take.
Left out: several people editing one page at the same moment (0018's revisit condition).

comments.author: claude-code:shady2k@vm-agents:main#916b13ad
comments.text: Owner, 2026-10-14: a good answer from this chat can be filed back into the wiki as a page or correction with its sources — see madarch-4n2c.

comments.author: claude-opus-5-5
comments.text:
Direction agreed with the owner, 2026-10-17 (~18:20 MSK), for the later milestone that takes this idea (not self-filling). Owner raised embedding DeepSeek Harness (https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, MIT, developer preview, unaudited per its SAFETY.md) and asked about the web UI: «А веб-интерфейс? Будем делать свою реализацию? Можно из openwebui или еще какого проекта взять?»; to the coordinator's proposal below: «Да».
- Agent link: madarch speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP, JSON-RPC over stdio) and runs agents as separate processes; dsh's `acp` profile is the first candidate default agent (its llm-pi-ai adapter reaches OpenAI-compatible gateways). Its code is not embedded in madarch (Node plugin tree, breaking changes expected; madarch is one Bun binary).
- UI: madarch's own panel beside the page built from ready components — assistant-ui (MIT, React/shadcn) or Vercel AI Elements (Apache-2.0, shadcn-style); a short side-by-side prototype decides between them before planning. Agent context: the page, the selected text, its open questions; proposed edits go through the same checked write path as answers and comments.
- Server-to-UI events in AG-UI (MIT) if it has settled by then, so the UI does not depend on which agent runs.
- Rejected: Open WebUI (standalone Python/Svelte chat app; its licence forbids removing its branding beyond 50 users in 30 days without an enterprise licence), LibreChat (standalone app), dsh's own web UI as madarch's UI (fine only for a throwaway prototype).

title: Lay the review report's problems on the diagrams in our own viewer
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-09-27, planning madarch-utk. Decision 0001 foresees our own viewer among the frontends; the MVP charter excludes it.

A viewer that shows the views and, on them, the model check's and the review report's findings: a cycle's arrows marked, an element whose document claim is stale greyed, a click on an element or arrow opening its evidence at its commit. The findings already name model ids (madarch-utk), so the report needs no rework for this.

Would show it is worth it: architects reading the review report ask where on the diagram a finding is.
Left out: editing the layout by hand (the vision excludes a canvas).

title: The slow server and model tests run well inside bun's per-test bound, or carry their own bound on purpose
description:
On the SkyPilot test pod (2 CPU / 4 GB, the machine every worker's tests run on since 2026-10-18), `test/server-graphs.test.ts` finishes each of its 31 tests in 2.5-5.6 s and bun's default per-test limit is 5 s, so a run of it times out at the margin rather than on a wrong result.

Measured on branch `feature/madarch-queue`, 2026-10-18, via `madarch-sky-test <worktree> test/server-graphs.test.ts`:
- with `test/server-sources.test.ts` in the same run: 111 pass, 2 fail — `a graph built from two sources > the union view holds both sources' roots, whose ids do not clash` timed out at 5575.70 ms and `shared query database ownership > removing one source from a union graph preserves the other source projection` at 5062.75 ms; the file's other tests in the same run took 2.5-4.9 s.
- alone, first rerun: 30 pass, 1 fail — the same union-view test timed out at 5010.67 ms (10 ms over the limit).
- alone, second rerun: all 31 pass; the pod was then OOM-killed (exit 137) at the end of the run.
CI's sharded test job has been green on both SHAs (`test shard 1-5` and `test`), so nothing is broken in the graph code: what is wrong is the margin.

## DONE WHEN
`test/server-graphs.test.ts` passes on the 2-CPU pod with at least 2x headroom under the limit it runs under: either the per-test time it needs is measured and the limit is raised with that measurement, or the work per test is cut (a smaller fixture, one shared database per file) so each test finishes well inside bun's default.

Disproved by: a run of that file on the pod timing out at the margin again.

## Left out
The other files of the same class already tracked (madarch-24sy.7) and the pod's memory limit (the exit-137 kill after the passing run is the pod's 4 GB, filed separately if it repeats).

comments.author: prime-coordinator:madarch@dev:chore/madarch-accept-stage-19#01a150f2
comments.text: More evidence, from the acceptance of stage madarch-tzte.19 (2026-10-19): the margin now bites CI too. CI run 39171437383, shard 2, failed on `a store that brings a clash into a built two-source graph drops its engine, and the next use refuses instead of answering with duplicate rows` at 5005 ms (limit 5000), while its neighbours in the same block took 3.0-3.5 s; the same SHA passed on the rerun. On the SkyPilot pod the same test failed at 5529 ms. The acceptance record of that stage names this as a pending limitation of its own evidence, not as its defect.

title: The engine reads nothing of the skill set by name: open questions, the audience, the stages' expected records and the record folders come from the product's manifest
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] The per-stage expected records live in the product manifest (docs/kinds.yaml) and are declared once; the skill set computes completeness, not madarch.
- [x] The contract defines the skill set's completeness result as a file under docs/ with a published schema and pinned conformance cases. The wiki renders that result when present and renders no completeness findings when absent.
- [x] The engine no longer computes missing completeness in src/wiki/stages.ts; it only renders the supplied result. The skill-set-side writer remains outside madarch-d7v3.2.
- [x] The completeness result is a committed docs/ file in the product repository and is treated as the truth at that commit’s time; its published schema includes the computed date and source revision, and the wiki displays the localized “as of” date without recomputing.
notes:
Owner decision 2026-10-13, relayed from the skill-set session (comment 2522): completeness is the skill set's calculation. This engine task updates the contract for per-stage expectations in docs/kinds.yaml and for the generated completeness file under docs/ (schema plus conformance cases), renders the file only when present, and removes madarch's src/wiki/stages.ts missing-completeness calculation. The skill-set writer task is external and remains out of scope.
Owner follow-up 2026-10-13 (newest source comment 2524): completeness is a committed product-repository docs/ snapshot at the commit’s time, not a live calculation. The schema must include the date and product revision it was computed for; the wiki presents the localized as-of date and never recomputes.

comments.text: The owner's rule restated (2026-10-13): 'Наш движок не должен содержать никаких данных. Если стартуем его с пустой папкой, то на главной показываем краткую инструкцию что делать.' So: no built-in stage list, no default kinds, groups, labels or expectations — everything the wiki shows of a product comes from the product's manifest and documents. The engine's own words are only its functions' UI (buttons, errors, the empty state). Started on an empty folder (no manifest, no documents), the home page shows a short instruction of what to do next (create a product with madarch new, or add a manifest; where the skill set fits). title: Make the query-engine long-run memory check independent of what ran before it in the same process
description:
Debt found 2026-10-09 during the madarch-rtr run (stage 1 acceptance), on this machine, while running
the project's full stage checks. It is pre-existing and off that feature's path; nothing in that
change touches the query engine or its tests.

## What was measured
`test/query-engine-long-run.test.ts` asserts the whole run stays under 400 MB
(`expect(Math.max(...curve)).toBeLessThan(400)`). That number is measured on the **process** that runs
it, so it depends on what ran before it in the same `bun test` process:

- the file alone: RSS 159-163 MB, curve flat (slope -0.14 MB/batch), passes;
- the same revision, `bun test test/query-engine-performance.test.ts test/query-engine-long-run.test.ts`
  in one process, perf file first: RSS 436-440 MB, curve flat (slope 0.05, thirds gap 0 MB), **fails**;
- the whole suite (`bun test`, 1234 tests across 55 files): RSS 608-620 MB, curve flat, **fails**.

In every case the shape is the bounded one the test exists to prove (a flat plateau, a small
prepared-statement cache); only the absolute level differs. CI on GitHub runners is green for the same
full suite.

## Why it matters
A required check that is red on the development machine while the file alone is green makes every
stage acceptance ambiguous: the reader cannot tell a real regression from the process's accumulated
allocations, which is exactly the case this test should decide.

## Done when
The check decides the same thing wherever it runs: its bound is measured against a baseline the check
itself establishes (RSS at the start of its own curve, or a bound per batch), or the long-run file is
run in its own process by the check that requires it, and the full suite is green on this machine.

  covers only what a change decides; `product.mjs where` answers about the folder it is started in).
  A second focused review of that answer confirmed the policy split and found one reversed sentence
  of mine, fixed at 2776b7e. No fallback reviewer was needed.
- Not run, and why: an actual GitHub Actions run (no runner is reachable here; each workflow's
  command was run locally on real revisions, and the CI wiring was read file by file); the full
  `bun test` suite and the wiki's real builds (`MADARCH_WIKI_E2E=1` only) — nothing the product
  reads changed since the 0.40.0 run proved them, and the focused test file and views:check were run
  again; the privacy guard's "no pattern list at all" branch (it needs removing the machine's user
  list, outside any scratch tree — the missing-file branch was proved instead); `tsc` inside the
  proof clones (no node_modules there; the pins and tsconfig's `include` are the evidence).
- Limits, named rather than hidden: the push entry point does not run the document gate
  (.shady2k/push.mjs:69-98 runs the commit links and the present-documents check), so the range that
  carries two changes is judged where documents.md judges it, per change — `documents.mjs` has no
  range mode, and the integration says so; `connect.sh` failed in one proof fixture clone at
  `br sync --migrate-source-repo-path` ("Issue madarch-pv1 has equal timestamps but divergent
  DB/JSONL payloads") because of rows that fixture had added by hand, and two other clean clones
  connected without it; and a wrong-but-parseable time in a record (for example `2026-02-30T…`) is
  invisible to `time-record-damaged`, which sees only what does not parse or a table that does not
  add up. This machine keeps a set state directory at ~/.local/state/shady2k-skills/ with other
  projects' run records and handoffs; madarch has none there, and nothing reads them now.

title: A connected code repository shows a wiki derived from its code at once, before any manifest or document is written
description:
Idea from the owner, 2026-10-14 ~23:55 MSK, after comparing madarch with Google Code Wiki, DeepWiki and Hermes code-wiki, Wiki Architect, the LLM Wiki Schema and product-architect. The owner doubted whether madarch is needed over code-only wikis; the agreed position: keep the core (intent linked to code across repositories, checked) and fix the value a person gets in the first minutes. Taken up after the standalone milestone's wiki-usable work, not into the current slice.

After `madarch repo add` (or opening a product with code repositories and no documents), the wiki shows pages derived from the code: architecture, modules, capabilities, entry points, each marked derived-from-code and each claim naming its file and line. Intent written later (vision, requirements, decisions) is layered over them and links to them; a derived page a person confirmed or corrected keeps that. Reference: Google Code Wiki and DeepWiki give value from code alone with zero setup.

Would show it is worth it: a person who connects a repository and writes nothing sees a usable wiki of it in the same session.
Left out: hosting for other people's public repositories; replacing the intended model.

comments.text:
Decision (gap closed alone), coordinator, 2026-10-08: the change makes a current requirement false unless the model history carries the new compiled arrays, so madarch-hnq.1.4 is added to stage 1 to close it.

What I found: src/history/assertions.ts decomposes a compiled model into one assertion per kind of seven (element, interface, relation, category, zone, environment, state) and assembles a model back from exactly those kinds. compiled-model/shape gains entities and scenarios (madarch-hnq.1.1, .1.2), so a compiled model holding them would be stored without them and would not read back as compiled — which is exactly what the current requirement model-history/lossless promises. The change's Coverage does not name model-history, and its Preserved contracts do not either, so this was an oversight in the change, not a decision against it.

Why I did not stop: the alternative closures both need the owner. Filing the limitation as debt and leaving model-history/lossless false would be a weaker acceptance, and correcting that spec sentence would be a new delta in the change record, which changes its approval digest and would need a fresh approval. Carrying the new arrays through the history keeps every present document true and leaves the change's decisions untouched.

What I decided: entities and scenarios are each source's exclusive claim, like elements, interfaces and relations (CLASHABLE_KINDS), not shared vocabulary like zones, categories, environments and states. A second source declaring an existing entity or scenario id is refused, naming the id and the other source; a data entity is a repository's own declaration of its data, and a use case is one repository's, so silently merging two declarations would be worse than refusing.

Where it lands: task madarch-hnq.1.4 under stage 1, after madarch-hnq.1.2, in src/history/** and src/adapters/**, with the change record's Tasks line extended (the Tasks line is not part of the approval digest, so the owner's approval of 2026-10-08 still stands; the feature document check is clean).

title: Close the stage-1 review findings in the model layer
description:
Change use-cases-data-entities, stage 1. The stage-1 review (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, 2026-10-08) found four valid defects in the model layer, all in this change's own new code:

1. src/model/compile.ts:213 compiles an entity whose `categories` the source left out to `categories: []`, erasing the difference between unchecked and explicitly uncategorised. The change's intended-model/entities scenario classification-not-stated says the compiled entity has no list of categories.
2. src/model/validate.ts:609 checks step ids unique within each flow separately, so a main-flow step and an alternative step may share an id; intended-model/ids says a step id is unique within its scenario.
3. src/model/compile.ts:74 rebuilds the entity-categories lookup once per relation, making compilation O(relations x entities); the intended-model performance requirement is under five seconds for 10 000 elements.
4. src/model/compiled-schema.ts:66 dropped the intended Transfer's minLength: 1 on confidentiality, so a compiled transfer with an empty confidentiality now validates.

## Done when
The four are fixed with tests; the published schemas are regenerated and committed; bun run check and the related suites pass; a mutation run on the changed ranges closes its survivors.
