title: Goals and maturity levels as manifest data: the engine's rules, levels, the home page's next goal and per-stage gaps
description:
Owner decision (2026-10-12 ~22:15 MSK, /tmp/madarch-run-iuc/note-goals-facts.md), second item: goals and maturity levels as MANIFEST DATA. v1 reserves the manifest section; the implementation is a later milestone item.

## Scope (later, deferring now)
- Rules over the graph: counts by type and status, required-link coverage, provenance agreement, approvals by role; grouped into levels per product and per role perspective (business, architecture, security, testing, ops).
- The engine computes progress on demand and shows on the home page "your next goal": one goal, why it matters, and a start-with-the-agent action.
- Per-stage completeness and the gaps: a requirement without an implementation, a service without an owner, a host without a security requirement, a document contradicted by code.
- The skill set ships default levels and goals, including brownfield goals: connect repositories, import docs, GitOps and diagrams, verify docs against code. A product may change them.
- Contract v1 reserves the manifest section so a product may carry goals data before the engine reads it (an engine without the section reads the rest and does not fail).

## DONE WHEN (when opened)
A served product with a goals manifest section shows the home page's next goal with its why and the start-with-the-agent action; per-stage completeness and the named gap kinds are computed on demand; the set's default levels install and a product's own levels override them; contract:check covers the section's refusals; review converged.

## Left out
Anything the v1 engine does not compute; approving the levels' exact default content; role-perspective views beyond the named five.

title: Connect a fresh clone with one committed command and sign commits with the owner's public email
description:
Found while connecting a clone on the owner's second computer (2026-09-24).

## Owner decision
Commits are signed with the owner's public email (the one shown on the GitHub profile), not the GitHub noreply address: it is already public, so hiding it buys nothing. The integration's rule 'Commits use the GitHub noreply address' and the fresh-clone step 'set user.email to the noreply address' change accordingly. Past noreply commits stay as they are.

## Problems
- Connecting a fresh clone is six manual steps listed in .shady2k/integration.md (hooks path, the br-portable-path filter, private patterns, br import and source-path migration). Git never applies repository config on clone, so this cannot be automatic, but it can be one committed command.
- The private pattern list lives only in .git/info/private-patterns of each clone, so a second machine starts without it.
- .githooks/privacy-guard.sh exits 0 when that file is missing: an unconnected clone passes any staged content silently.

## Done when
- one committed command connects a fresh clone (hooks path, filter, br import and path migration, private patterns) and is idempotent on a connected one;
- the guard reads patterns from .git/info/private-patterns and from a documented per-user location outside the repository (synced by the owner), and refuses a commit, saying how to connect, when neither exists;
- the integration states the public-email rule and names the command as the fresh-clone step;
- proved on a fresh clone: before connecting, a commit is refused with the connect hint; after connecting, the hooks reject planted violations.

## Left out
No global git config is written by the command; syncing the pattern file between machines is the owner's own tooling.
close_reason: Done by the setup 0.26.0 update (madarch-kwe): sh .shady2k/connect.sh connects a fresh clone and is safe to rerun; the privacy guard reads a per-user and a per-clone list and refuses without one; the integration states the public-email rule and names the command; proved on fresh clones.

title: The product overview tells a reader what the product is, for whom, its vision and where it stands, before any list of document groups
description:
What a person does: opens the wiki's home page (Product overview). What happens: a count ('23 documents in 17 groups'), one audience line, then boxes per group (PRODUCT, ARCHITECTURE, CAPABILITIES...) listing titles. What should happen: a product manager or an architect learns on that page what the product is, for whom, the vision's problem and outcome, the current milestone and its state, and where to go next; the group lists come after, or elsewhere. Owner: 'На главной странице что такое обзор продукта и просто набор каких-то меню непонятных … Что он здесь увидит?'
## DONE WHEN
On the demo product and on madarch's own product wiki, the home page's first screen names the product, its audience, the problem and outcome from the vision, the current milestone with its state and a next step, each from the product's documents; a test pins it.
## Left out
The group navigation itself (sidebar).

The owner, 2026-10-13, on the served demo wiki (Fieldnote): "Получается, что это неюзабельно сейчас."
close_reason: Accepted on rendered madarch-product and empty-folder English/Russian reader walk; Fieldnote is superseded by the owner-approved n5ip demo change. Missing authoritative ten-case list recorded as limitation; mutation deferred under Addendum 11.

title: A reader comments on selected text in the wiki; the discussion stands in the margin, is kept in the product's git and is in the graph
description:
A reader selects text on a wiki page, writes a comment, and the discussion stands in the margin beside that text; the comment is kept in the product's git and is in the graph.

Taken into the standalone milestone by the owner on 2026-10-14 ("Пока мы ждем, нужно реализовать добавление комментария"); design agreed in conversation the same day. Storage follows decision 0017 ("Comments and discussions are kept in git beside their page", one write path) and 0023 (authored data: truth in the product's git; the graph is a derived index).

## Agreed design
- UI (as Google Docs, Notion, Confluence): selecting text offers "Комментировать"; the thread card stands in the right margin level with its text, the text is highlighted, hover links card and text both ways; replies; resolve (resolved hidden, can be shown); a page-level comment without a selection; on a narrow screen the margin folds into a discussions panel.
- Anchor (owner: the mark is on the selection, not a point): two invisible markers wrap the selected range in the Markdown source, `<!--c:<id>-->selected text<!--/c:<id>-->` (HTML comments: hidden on GitHub and in the wiki). They move with the text; edits inside keep the range. The rendered selection is mapped to source positions through the parser's position data; a selection crossing an inline construct's boundary widens to whole words and elements so markers never break the markup. Overlapping ranges with different ids are allowed.
- The discussion lives outside the document: one file per message, `comments/<thread id>/<message id>.md` (Markdown with a front matter: author, time, thread, anchor quote with 32 characters around it, the document path and the commit it was made on, status); ids are ULIDs. Replies never touch the document. The document changes twice: the first comment inserts the markers, resolving removes them.
- Lost anchors: a deleted range (both markers gone) puts its thread in a "к изменённому тексту" list with its saved quote; one marker missing is refused by the document check, and the wiki restores the end by the saved quote or asks to place it again.
- Write path: the wiki server writes the files and commits at once as the author (git's user locally), one commit per action so any one is undone alone; then pushes at once (owner: yes); on a rejected push it pulls and retries; when that fails the comment shows "не отправлено" and is retried.
- Graph: a thread is an element of madarch's own kind `discussion` (generic Element/Relation tables, no new table), with relation `about` to the document's element (and to the model element the document is, where it is one), properties status, anchor quote, authors, created and last activity; messages are not nodes (their text goes to full-text search). Rebuilt from git like every index (0023). Room kept for the tracker (madarch-lk4r): a thread may later link to a work item.
- The comment files' layout and the marker syntax join the product-repository contract (a schema version and cases), so the skill set's agents read and answer threads through the same write path.

## Done when
- In a browser, on a served product: select text, comment, see the card in the margin and the highlight; reply; resolve; page-level comment; reload shows the same; the narrow-screen panel works. A built-app E2E test covers these with screenshots.
- The product repository holds the markers and message files exactly as above, one commit per action, pushed; a rejected push is retried and a failed one shows "не отправлено".
- Editing inside, around and through a range behaves as the design says (fixture tests), and the document check refuses an unpaired marker with file and line.
- The graph answers "open discussions about document X" and "documents with open discussions".
- Left out: editing and deleting messages, mentions and notifications, server-mode users and permissions, linking to tracker items.

title: A reader can add a comment to selected text and see it beside the page
description:
## Done when
On a served fixture product, a reader selects valid text on a wiki page, chooses “Comment”, writes a message, and saves. The selected source range gains matching hidden markers; a ULID message file is written at `comments/<thread ULID>/<message ULID>.md` with contract-v1 metadata, quote/context and body. The comment is shown beside its anchor, and reload shows the same comment and anchor. The save produces one git commit per action and pushes it; a rejected push follows the agreed pull-and-retry path, and a final failure is shown as not sent without losing the retryable message. The document check accepts the saved pair and refuses a broken pair with file and line. Browser E2E evidence covers the entire path on a fixture product; all checks and review pass.

## Scope
First-comment vertical slice only: selection-to-source mapping, selection-safe marker insertion, message creation, the server write endpoint and the comment card/highlight needed to show the saved result. Keep all writes inside the selected product repository and follow discussion v1. No replies, resolving, editing/deleting messages, tracker links, permissions or graph indexing in this stage.

## Why this stage first
It makes the feature's main path reachable and exercises the complete ownership boundary from browser selection through the product repository, before adding thread actions or a derived graph.

title: Readers can reply, resolve and recover changed discussion anchors
description:
## Done when
On a served product, a reader can open discussions at a page-level anchor, reply to an existing thread, resolve it and show resolved discussions again. Each action is stored as the required per-message file and a separate git commit/push; reloading preserves the thread state. A deleted selection range is shown as a lost anchor with its saved quote; the wiki can restore the end by the saved quote or ask the reader to place it again. The discussion margin works at desktop width and folds into the discussions panel at narrow width. Fixture tests cover edits inside, around and through a marked range; the document check rejects an unpaired marker with path and line. Full checks and review pass.

## Scope
Thread actions, page-level comments, lost-anchor recovery/display, responsive margin/panel, and browser coverage. Editing/deleting messages, mentions, notifications, server-mode users/permissions and tracker links remain out of scope.

## Prerequisite
Build on the accepted first-comment vertical slice so the thread display and write path already exist.

title: Open discussions are searchable through the derived graph
description:
## Done when
After rebuilding the derived graph from a fixture product repository, it contains each discussion thread as a `discussion` element related with `about` to its document, with the specified status, quote, authors, creation and last-activity properties. Messages are not graph elements. Queries return open discussions about a named document and documents with open discussions, and results agree with the checked-in fixture files. Rebuilding after a git change updates the derived graph without changing the authored product files. Full checks and review pass.

## Scope
Graph ingestion/projection and query coverage for discussion threads only, using the existing graph element/relation model and the decisions 0023/0024. No new storage table and no tracker linkage.

## Prerequisite
The discussion message and marker behavior must be accepted, so indexing consumes the stable repository contract and write results.

title: The compiled binary's build smoke passes again since madarch new started a background server, and new's --port is honoured or refused, not ignored
description:
Found by the coordinator 2026-10-18 while landing PR #77. ## What happens The "clean install walks" workflow (`.github/workflows/clean-installs.yml`) has failed on every push to main since `ea42ed10` (PR #65, madarch-zcti.1, 2026-10-17 18:02 UTC); the last green run is `ddf3e76b`. The jobs build-linux-fixture, macos-arm64 and windows-x64 fail in `bun scripts/build-binary.ts` with "the built binary could not create a draft, open the graph store and serve it (exit 0)" (run 39131966606, job 117688793645). Since madarch-zcti.1, `madarch new --home --port

--no-open` returns at once after starting the background server, and that server listens on a port of its own: the run printed `http://127.0.0.1:32993/products/idea-2026-10-18/` while the smoke polled the random port it passed (`scripts/build-binary.ts:150-173`). The smoke never sees the product, and the background server it started is never stopped. ## What should happen A person who passes `--port` to `madarch new` either gets the wiki on that port or is told plainly why not; a flag silently ignored is a defect.
